meta.description: This program allows bank staff to search for and display the details of a specific credit card by entering an account number and/or card number as search criteria.
meta.process_description: The program presents a search screen where bank staff can enter an account number (11 digits) and optionally a card number (16 digits) to locate a specific credit card record. It validates the entered search criteria, ensuring the account number is a non-zero numeric value and the card number, if provided, is a valid 16-digit numeric value. Upon successful validation, it retrieves the matching credit card details from the card database and displays them on screen, including card number, cardholder name, CVV, expiry date, and card status. The program integrates with a card list program (COCRDLIC) to support navigation from a list view to a detail view, and allows users to exit back to the calling program or main menu via PF3.

files.CARDDAT: Primary credit card data file storing full card details including card number, account linkage, cardholder name, CVV, expiry date and card status
files.CARDAIX: Alternate index path on the card data file allowing card records to be retrieved by account ID rather than card number

business_rules: Account number is mandatory and must be an 11-digit non-zero numeric value; blank or zero account numbers are rejected with an appropriate error message.
Card number is optional, but if supplied it must be a valid 16-digit numeric value; non-numeric or incorrectly sized card numbers are rejected.
At least one search criterion (account number) must be provided; submitting the screen with no input is not permitted.
If the account number does not exist in the card cross-reference database, an error is displayed indicating no cards were found for that account.
If the combination of account number and card number does not match any record, the user is informed that no cards were found for the given search condition.
Pressing PF3 exits the program and returns the user to the previously calling program or the main menu if no calling program is recorded.
When navigating from the card list screen (COCRDLIC), the account and card number are passed automatically and card details are retrieved without requiring manual re-entry.
Only the Enter key and PF3 are treated as valid function keys; any other key press is treated as an Enter key action to prevent unintended navigation.

variables.name: WS-MISC-STORAGE
variables.description: Top-level working storage group that holds all temporary variables used during the card search process, including CICS processing state, input validation flags, card data output fields, file error details, and user-facing messages.

variables.name: WS-CICS-PROCESSNG-VARS
variables.description: Group of variables used to capture the outcome of CICS service calls (such as file reads), enabling the program to detect and handle system-level errors during card data retrieval.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The primary CICS response code returned after a file operation (e.g. reading the card or account file). A non-zero value indicates that the card lookup did not complete successfully, triggering an error message to bank staff.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The secondary CICS reason code that provides additional detail about why a file operation failed. Used alongside WS-RESP-CD to give a more precise diagnosis when a card record cannot be retrieved.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The 4-character CICS transaction identifier for the current card search screen. Used to identify which transaction is running and to support correct screen navigation and program linking.

variables.name: WS-INPUT-FLAG
variables.description: Overall input validation status flag for the card search screen. Tracks whether the bank staff's entered search criteria (account number and/or card number) have passed all validation checks, failed validation, or are still awaiting initial entry.

variables.name: INPUT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that all search criteria entered by the bank staff have passed validation and the card lookup can proceed.

variables.name: INPUT-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that one or more search criteria entered by the bank staff have failed validation (e.g. non-numeric account number, invalid card number length), and an error message must be displayed before the search can proceed.

variables.name: INPUT-PENDING
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank staff has not yet submitted any search criteria — the screen has just been displayed for the first time and is awaiting initial input.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ACCT-FLAG
variables.description: Validation status flag specifically for the account number field. Records whether the account number entered by the bank staff is valid, invalid, or has been left blank, driving the appropriate error or search behaviour.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account number entered by the bank staff has failed validation (e.g. it is non-numeric, zero, or not 11 digits), and the search cannot proceed until it is corrected.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account number entered by the bank staff has passed all validation rules and is acceptable as a search key to look up credit card records.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank staff left the account number field empty. Since account number is mandatory, this triggers a prompt requiring the staff member to enter a valid account number before searching.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CARD-FLAG
variables.description: Validation status flag specifically for the card number field. Records whether the optional card number entered by the bank staff is valid, invalid, or has been left blank, allowing the search to be filtered to a specific card or broadened to all cards on the account.

variables.name: FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card number entered by the bank staff has failed validation (e.g. it is non-numeric or not exactly 16 digits), and must be corrected before the search can proceed.

variables.name: FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card number entered by the bank staff has passed all validation rules and can be used as an additional filter to narrow the card search to a specific card on the account.

variables.name: FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank staff left the card number field empty. Since card number is optional, this is acceptable and the search will return all cards associated with the given account number.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG
variables.description: Flag that controls whether the program should return control to the calling program (e.g. the card list screen or main menu) rather than continuing to display the card search screen. Set when the bank staff presses PF3 to exit.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank staff has not requested to exit the card search screen; the program should continue processing normally.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG-ON
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank staff has pressed PF3 to exit, and the program should transfer control back to the previously calling program or the main menu.

variables.name: WS-PFK-FLAG
variables.description: Flag that records whether the function key pressed by the bank staff is a recognised and permitted key (Enter or PF3). Any unrecognised key press is treated as invalid and the flag is set accordingly to prevent unintended navigation.

variables.name: PFK-VALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank staff pressed a recognised function key (Enter or PF3), and the program should process the corresponding action (search or exit).

variables.name: PFK-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the bank staff pressed an unrecognised function key. The program treats this as an Enter key press to prevent accidental navigation away from the card search screen.

variables.name: CICS-OUTPUT-EDIT-VARS
variables.description: Group of working storage fields that hold the credit card details retrieved from the card data file, ready to be formatted and displayed to the bank staff on the card detail screen.

variables.name: CARD-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: The 11-digit account number associated with the retrieved credit card, held as a character string for display purposes on the card detail screen.

variables.name: CARD-ACCT-ID-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the account number field, allowing the program to perform numeric comparisons or arithmetic on the account ID when validating or processing the card record.

variables.name: CARD-CVV-CD-X
variables.description: The 3-digit Card Verification Value (CVV) security code of the retrieved credit card, held as a character string for display to authorised bank staff on the card detail screen.

variables.name: CARD-CVV-CD-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the CVV field, allowing the program to validate that the CVV contains only numeric digits before displaying it.

variables.name: CARD-CARD-NUM-X
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number of the retrieved card, held as a character string for display on the card detail screen and for matching against the optional card number filter entered by the bank staff.

variables.name: CARD-CARD-NUM-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the card number field, used to validate that the card number is entirely numeric and non-zero before accepting it as a valid search filter.

variables.name: CARD-NAME-EMBOSSED-X
variables.description: The cardholder's name exactly as it is embossed on the physical credit card, retrieved from the card record and displayed to bank staff on the card detail screen for identity verification purposes.

variables.name: CARD-STATUS-X
variables.description: The current operational status of the retrieved credit card (e.g. active, inactive, blocked), displayed to bank staff so they can assess whether the card is usable by the cardholder.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE-X
variables.description: The expiry date of the retrieved credit card in YYYY-MM-DD format, displayed to bank staff to confirm whether the card is still within its valid period.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Structural redefinition of the card expiry date field that breaks it into its individual year, month, and day components, allowing the program to access or validate each part of the expiry date separately (e.g. to check if the card has expired).

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRY-YEAR
variables.description: The 4-digit year component of the credit card's expiry date (e.g. 2026), extracted from the full expiry date to allow individual date component processing or display.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The separator character (hyphen) between the year and month components of the card expiry date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Not displayed independently; purely structural.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRY-MONTH
variables.description: The 2-digit month component of the credit card's expiry date (e.g. 09 for September), extracted from the full expiry date to allow individual date component processing or display.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The separator character (hyphen) between the month and day components of the card expiry date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Not displayed independently; purely structural.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRY-DAY
variables.description: The 2-digit day component of the credit card's expiry date (e.g. 30), extracted from the full expiry date to allow individual date component processing or display.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the full card expiry date field, allowing the program to perform numeric comparisons on the date (e.g. to determine whether the card has already expired relative to today's date).

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID
variables.description: The record identifier (RID) structure used to locate a specific credit card record in the card data file. Combines the card number and account ID to form the composite key used when reading from the CARDDAT or CARDAIX file.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number portion of the file record identifier, used as the primary key when reading a specific card record directly from the CARDDAT file.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The 11-digit account number portion of the file record identifier, used as the alternate index key when reading card records via the CARDAIX file to retrieve all cards linked to a given account.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: Character reinterpretation of the account ID within the record identifier, allowing the account number to be treated as a string when constructing or comparing file keys during the card lookup.

variables.name: WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE
variables.description: A structured diagnostic message assembled when a file operation (such as reading the card data file) fails. Combines the operation name, file name, and CICS response codes into a single readable message to help support staff diagnose the cause of a card retrieval failure.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed label text at the start of the file error message (e.g. 'FILE ERROR: '), providing context for the error details that follow. Not a data value; purely presentational.

variables.name: ERROR-OPNAME
variables.description: The name of the file operation that failed (e.g. 'READ', 'STARTBR'), included in the error message to help support staff identify at which point in the card search process the failure occurred.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Spacing or label text between the operation name and file name in the error message. Purely presentational.

variables.name: ERROR-FILE
variables.description: The name of the file that could not be accessed (e.g. 'CARDDAT' or 'CARDAIX'), included in the error message so support staff know which data source failed during the card search.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Spacing or label text between the file name and the CICS response code in the error message. Purely presentational.

variables.name: ERROR-RESP
variables.description: The primary CICS response code formatted as text and included in the error message, allowing support staff to identify the category of error that prevented the card record from being retrieved.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Spacing or label text between the primary and secondary CICS response codes in the error message. Purely presentational.

variables.name: ERROR-RESP2
variables.description: The secondary CICS reason code formatted as text and included in the error message, providing additional detail about the specific cause of the file access failure during the card search.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing spacing at the end of the file error message. Purely presentational.

variables.name: WS-LONG-MSG
variables.description: A large free-text buffer used to hold extended diagnostic or informational messages during card search processing, for example when constructing detailed error descriptions for logging or display to support staff.

variables.name: WS-INFO-MSG
variables.description: A short informational message displayed to bank staff indicating the outcome of the card search, such as confirming that card details are being shown, prompting for input, or indicating that no cards were found for the account.

variables.name: WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that there is no informational message to display to the bank staff — the info message area on the screen should be left blank.

variables.name: FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card search was successful and card details have been found for the given account number, prompting the program to display the card detail information to the bank staff.

variables.name: WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card search screen is prompting the bank staff to enter search criteria (account number and optionally card number) before a search can be performed.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG
variables.description: A user-facing validation or status message displayed to bank staff on the card search screen, describing input errors (e.g. 'Account number must be 11 digits') or the result of the search (e.g. 'No cards found for this account'), guiding them to correct their input or understand the search outcome.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that no return message is currently set for display to bank staff — the message area is blank, meaning no validation error or status prompt is active.

variables.name: WS-EXIT-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the program is displaying a farewell or exit message to the bank staff member, typically shown when the user presses PF3 to leave the card search screen.

variables.name: WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the program is prompting the bank staff member to enter a valid account number, because none was provided or the one entered was invalid.

variables.name: WS-PROMPT-FOR-CARD
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the program is prompting the bank staff member to enter a valid card number, because the card number supplied failed validation (e.g. non-numeric or wrong length).

variables.name: NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the bank staff member submitted the search screen without entering any search criteria — neither an account number nor a card number was provided. The search cannot proceed and the user must be prompted to supply at least an account number.

variables.name: SEARCHED-ACCT-ZEROES
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the account number entered by the bank staff member was all zeros, which is not a valid account identifier. The search is rejected and the user is asked to provide a real account number.

variables.name: SEARCHED-ACCT-NOT-NUMERIC
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the account number entered by the bank staff member contained non-numeric characters and therefore cannot be used to search for a credit card record. The user must re-enter a valid 11-digit numeric account number.

variables.name: SEARCHED-CARD-NOT-NUMERIC
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the card number entered by the bank staff member contained non-numeric characters or was not a valid 16-digit number. The user must correct the card number before the search can proceed.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-CARDXREF
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the account number entered by the bank staff member does not exist in the card cross-reference database (CARDAIX). No credit cards are linked to this account, and an appropriate 'not found' message is displayed to the user.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-ACCTCARD-COMBO
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that while the account number exists, the specific combination of account number and card number entered by the bank staff member does not match any credit card record. The user is informed that no card was found for the given search criteria.

variables.name: XREF-READ-ERROR
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that an unexpected system error occurred while attempting to read the card cross-reference file (CARDAIX or CARDDAT). This signals a technical failure rather than a business validation issue, and an error message is displayed to the bank staff member.

variables.name: CODING-TO-BE-DONE
variables.description: Condition flag used as a development placeholder to mark a program state or code path that has not yet been fully implemented. This should not be triggered in a production environment and indicates incomplete functionality.

variables.name: WS-LITERALS
variables.description: Group record holding all fixed constant values used by the card search program — including program names, transaction IDs, map names and file names — so that these identifiers are defined in one place and can be referenced consistently throughout the program logic.

variables.name: LIT-THISPGM
variables.description: The fixed name of this program (COCRDSLC), used when the program needs to identify itself — for example, when recording navigation history or passing control back to a calling program.

variables.name: LIT-THISTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID associated with this card search program. Used when initiating or returning to this transaction within the CardDemo application flow.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAPSET
variables.description: The name of the BMS mapset that contains the screen layout for the card search display. Used to send or receive the correct screen definition when presenting the card detail search form to bank staff.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAP
variables.description: The name of the specific BMS map (screen) within the mapset that defines the layout of the card search input and results screen shown to bank staff.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTPGM
variables.description: The program name of the credit card list screen (COCRDLIC). Used when navigating back to the card list after viewing card details, ensuring the correct program is invoked for back-navigation.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the credit card list screen. Used to transfer control back to the card list transaction when the bank staff member exits the card detail view.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the credit card list screen. Referenced when the program needs to direct the user back to the card list display.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name for the credit card list screen. Used to render the correct screen layout when returning the bank staff member to the list of cards.

variables.name: LIT-MENUPGM
variables.description: The program name of the CardDemo main menu. Used when the bank staff member presses PF3 and there is no specific calling program recorded, so the system returns the user to the main menu.

variables.name: LIT-MENUTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the CardDemo main menu. Used to initiate the main menu transaction when the bank staff member exits the card search screen with no prior calling program.

variables.name: LIT-MENUMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the CardDemo main menu screen. Referenced when navigating the user back to the main menu upon exit.

variables.name: LIT-MENUMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name for the CardDemo main menu screen. Used to display the correct main menu layout when the bank staff member exits the card search program.

variables.name: LIT-CARDFILENAME
variables.description: The CICS file name for the primary credit card data file (CARDDAT), which stores full card details including card number, cardholder name, CVV, expiry date and card status. Used when reading card records directly by card number.

variables.name: LIT-CARDFILENAME-ACCT-PATH
variables.description: The CICS file name for the alternate index path on the card data file (CARDAIX), which allows card records to be retrieved by account ID rather than card number. Used when the bank staff member searches by account number.

variables.name: WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA
variables.description: Working storage communication area specific to this card search program, used to retain context about which program or transaction called this screen so that back-navigation works correctly when the bank staff member exits.

variables.name: CA-CALL-CONTEXT
variables.description: Group of fields that together identify the origin of the call to this card search program — recording which program and transaction transferred control here, enabling correct return navigation.

variables.name: CA-FROM-PROGRAM
variables.description: The name of the program that called this card search screen (e.g. the card list program COCRDLIC or the main menu). Stored so that when the bank staff member presses PF3, the system knows which program to return control to.

variables.name: CA-FROM-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID of the calling program or screen. Retained alongside the calling program name to ensure the correct transaction is re-initiated when the bank staff member exits the card search screen.

variables.name: WS-COMMAREA
variables.description: A 2000-byte working storage buffer used to hold a copy of the CICS communication area (COMMAREA) passed between programs. This allows the card search program to read data passed from a calling program — such as a pre-populated account ID from the card list screen — and to pass data forward to the next program in the navigation flow.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The standard CICS communication area (COMMAREA) through which data is exchanged between programs in the CardDemo application. When the card search program is called from another screen (e.g. the card list), this area carries context such as the account ID and card number so the search can be pre-populated automatically without requiring the bank staff member to re-enter information.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A placeholder byte within the DFHCOMMAREA structure with no direct business meaning. It ensures the communication area is correctly aligned and sized for CICS inter-program data passing, even when the full COMMAREA content is mapped elsewhere (e.g. via WS-COMMAREA).

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.description: This is the main orchestration paragraph that controls the entire credit card search and display process. It determines the program's entry context, validates the function key pressed, and routes the session to the appropriate action — whether that is exiting to a previous screen, displaying a blank search form, retrieving card details passed from the card list screen, or processing manually entered search criteria.

paragraphs.name: COMMON-RETURN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph finalises the current screen interaction and hands control back to the CICS transaction manager, preserving any validation or status messages and the full application session state so the next screen or program can continue seamlessly. It acts as the single, consistent exit point for the credit card search program regardless of what action triggered the return.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the main processing routine for the credit card search program. It marks the end of the main business logic flow, allowing control to return cleanly to the CICS transaction manager after all search, validation, and display operations have completed.

paragraphs.name: 1000-SEND-MAP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full preparation and delivery of the credit card search screen to the bank staff member, coordinating all steps from initialising the display through to presenting the final screen with card details or validation messages.

paragraphs.name: 1000-SEND-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the map-sending routine, marking the end of the screen display process. It acts as a structural boundary that signals the completion of any screen output operation before control returns to the calling logic.

paragraphs.name: 1100-SCREEN-INIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph initialises the credit card search screen by clearing any previously displayed data and populating the screen header with standard identifying information, including the current date and time, so that bank staff see a clean, correctly labelled screen ready for input.

paragraphs.name: 1100-SCREEN-INIT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen initialisation routine, marking the end of the screen setup process before the program proceeds to handle user interaction. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural boundary within the credit card search screen workflow.

paragraphs.name: 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares the credit card search screen for display by populating it with the appropriate search criteria and retrieved card details. It also ensures that a meaningful prompt or status message is always shown to the bank staff member viewing the screen.

paragraphs.name: 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen variable setup routine. It acts as a structural placeholder marking the end of the screen initialisation process, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling logic after all display fields have been prepared.

paragraphs.name: 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph configures the visual presentation of the credit card search screen by controlling which fields are editable, where the cursor is positioned to guide data entry, and how fields are colour-coded to highlight validation errors or missing input to bank staff.

paragraphs.name: 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a placeholder exit point for the screen attribute setup routine. It marks the end of the screen configuration logic, allowing the program to return control to the calling section after any screen field formatting has been completed.

paragraphs.name: 1400-SEND-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph renders the credit card search/detail screen to the bank staff member's terminal, displaying the current state of the screen including any search results, validation messages, or prompts for input. It ensures the screen is fully refreshed and the keyboard is unlocked so the user can continue interacting with the application.

paragraphs.name: 1400-SEND-SCREEN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen-sending routine, marking the end of the process that presents the credit card search screen to bank staff. It acts as a structural boundary in the program flow, ensuring control returns cleanly to the calling logic after the screen has been dispatched.

paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full input processing cycle for the credit card search screen: it collects what the bank staff entered, validates the search criteria, and prepares the program to redisplay the same search screen with any resulting error or status messages.

paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the input processing routine, marking the end of the search criteria validation and input handling phase before the program proceeds to retrieve and display card details.

paragraphs.name: 2100-RECEIVE-MAP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the search criteria entered by bank staff on the credit card search screen, reading the account number and optional card number submitted by the user into the program for subsequent validation and processing.

paragraphs.name: 2100-RECEIVE-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the map-receiving routine, which handles the capture of search criteria entered by bank staff on the credit card search screen. It acts as a structural placeholder marking the end of that input-capture process.

paragraphs.name: 2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the search criteria entered by bank staff before attempting to retrieve credit card records. It clears any previous validation state, normalises the entered account and card number inputs, triggers individual field validation checks, and detects whether the staff member has submitted the search form without entering any search criteria at all.

paragraphs.name: 2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the input validation routine, marking the end of the process that checks whether the account number and card number entered by bank staff meet the required business rules before a card search is performed.

paragraphs.name: 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the account number entered by bank staff on the credit card search screen. It ensures the account number is present, numeric, and correctly formatted before allowing the search to proceed.

paragraphs.name: 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account number validation routine, marking the end of the account editing and validation process before control returns to the calling logic.

paragraphs.name: 2220-EDIT-CARD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the optional credit card number filter entered by bank staff on the search screen. It ensures the card number is either left blank (acceptable, as it is optional) or is a valid 16-digit numeric value before allowing the search to proceed.

paragraphs.name: 2220-EDIT-CARD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card input validation routine, signalling that all validation checks on the entered account and card number have been completed and control can return to the calling process.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-DATA
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the retrieval of a specific credit card record from the card database using the account number and optional card number provided by the bank staff. It delegates the actual data lookup to a dedicated sub-process that searches for a matching card record.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-DATA-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card data retrieval routine, signalling that the process of reading credit card details from the database has concluded and control should return to the calling logic.

paragraphs.name: 9100-GETCARD-BYACCTCARD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph attempts to retrieve a specific credit card record from the card database using the card number as the lookup key. Based on the outcome, it either confirms the card was found or flags an appropriate error to inform bank staff that the account/card combination does not exist or that a system-level read failure occurred.

paragraphs.name: 9100-GETCARD-BYACCTCARD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card retrieval routine that searches for a credit card record by account number and card number. It marks the end of the lookup process, returning control to whichever part of the program invoked the search.

paragraphs.name: 9150-GETCARD-BYACCT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph attempts to retrieve a credit card record from the card database using the account number as the search key, via the alternate index path. Based on the outcome, it either confirms the card was found or flags an error condition for the user.

paragraphs.name: 9150-GETCARD-BYACCT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the routine that retrieves credit card details by account number, returning control to the calling logic once the card lookup process is complete. It contains no active business logic and acts purely as a structural boundary marker for the card retrieval subroutine.

paragraphs.name: SEND-LONG-TEXT
paragraphs.description: Displays a full-screen plain-text message to the bank staff member, typically used to communicate a critical system or error condition, then immediately ends the program session and returns control to CICS.

paragraphs.name: SEND-LONG-TEXT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a placeholder exit point for a plain-text screen sending routine. It is explicitly marked as not suitable for production use, indicating it is a development or debugging stub only.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PLAIN-TEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the display of a plain-text error or status message to the bank staff member when a full screen refresh is not appropriate. It presents the message and immediately ends the program session, returning control to CICS.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PLAIN-TEXT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the plain-text screen sending routine, marking the end of that process. It also incorporates shared logic to capture and store which function key the bank staff pressed, enabling the program to correctly interpret the user's intended navigation action.

paragraphs.name: ABEND-ROUTINE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles unrecoverable system failures within the credit card search program, ensuring that a meaningful error message is recorded and displayed to bank staff before the program is forcibly terminated. It acts as a last-resort safety net to prevent silent failures and ensure auditability of unexpected crashes.
